reason: For every slot of an `Identifier`, `Namespace`, `QualifiedName`, two `Literal` values and a default `Namespace`, `setattr` and `delattr` raise `AttributeError` "Class.field is read-only", and the value, hash and text stay unchanged. #444, which enforces immutability of these classes.

A document with a default namespace and one entity, pickled under each protocol, loads with a default namespace of prefix `""` and the same IRI, and equals the original. #649, whose upgrade-page row says a default namespace is set only through `set_default_namespace()` and a `Namespace` with an empty prefix is refused.

A subclass of each class can set, change and delete its own attribute, still refuses assignment and deletion of an inherited field, and an instance attribute named `_READ_ONLY` does not lift the guard. #444.
`copy.copy` and `copy.deepcopy` of each value equal the original. The 3.2.1 entry in `HISTORY.md`, which says these classes keep working under copy and pickle.

An `Identifier` and a `QualifiedName` at the same URI are equal and hash to `hash("http://example.org/e1")`. The 3.2.1 spec section 2.1, which states `hash(Identifier(u)) == hash(ns[local])` when the URIs match.

`qn._uri = "x"` carries `type: ignore[misc]` and `undeclared` assignments to a `QualifiedName`, a `Namespace` and a `Literal` carry `type: ignore[attr-defined]`, and each raises `AttributeError`. #444, which makes the fields final. The module is not on the mypy override list, so mypy checks the `type: ignore` comments and fails the gate if the annotations stop raising those errors.

With `_CACHE_LIMIT` set to 3, `Namespace._cache` holds names in lookup order, a rejected local part leaves the full cache unchanged, a miss at the limit empties the cache, and a name taken before the flush equals and hashes as the one taken after it. Spec 5 section 4.5 (#694), which bounds the namespace cache and picks the flush policy.

Asserts `NS["e1"] is NS["e1"]`, the identity of a repeated `Namespace.__getitem__` lookup. Spec 5 section 4.5 (#694) calls the namespace cache behaviour-free and says no code relies on that identity, so the test pins an incidental detail. The maintainer recorded it as `rewrite`, like the two other identity tests the same audit recorded. The test does not change.

An `Identifier`, `Namespace`, `QualifiedName` and two `Literal` values have no `__dict__`, and assigning an undeclared attribute raises `AttributeError`. The 3.2.1 spec section 2.1 and the 3.2.1 entry in `HISTORY.md`, which add `__slots__` to the four value classes.

`__setstate__` with a 3.2.0-style `(None, slots)` tuple loads an `Identifier`, `QualifiedName`, `Namespace` and `Literal` equal to the originals with the same hash. The `HISTORY.md` 3.2.1 entry, which says 3.2.0 pickles load.

A `QualifiedName` pickled by a subprocess under hash seeds 12345 and 54321 loads equal to a fresh one with the same hash, and finds the fresh name's dictionary entry. The 3.2.1 spec section 2.1 and its `HISTORY.md` entry, which say an unpickled object recomputes its hash in the loading process.
